title: Shard prioritizer and failure-compressor: probe orchestration + CI bridge
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds shard-based probe prioritization and a failure-compression layer to reduce noisy CI alerts. New metric (reliability_score) and CI adapter to rate-limit retriggers. Backwards-compatible with existing probe configs.
description: Motivation: our long-running prompt suites produce large numbers of noisy failures that drown signal and cause frequent engineer interrupt loops. This PR implements two complementary pieces: 1) a shard prioritizer that assigns probe shards (cohorts/prompt-sets) priority scores based on recent instability, historical importance, and latency impact; priority influences sampling frequency and scheduling so that high-risk prompt shards get probed earlier in CI windows; 2) a failure-compressor that groups identical or near-identical failures into envelope signatures (text-normalized message, canonical stack, metric deltas) and emits a single canonical incident summary to the CI reporter. Together these reduce noisy duplicates and improve the signal-to-noise ratio for regression alerts. The PR also wires a new reliability_score metric used by the CI bridge to make retry/attenuation decisions and introduces a small CI adapter that performs rate-limited retries for transient failures and suppresses repeated signatures for a configurable cooldown window. Backwards compatibility: existing probe configs continue to work; the new prioritizer is opt-in via eval_config.prioritization.enabled. Changes include: scheduler refactor to add shard metadata, a lightweight LRU signature cache for compression, metric emitter for reliability_score, a CLI flag (--shard-prioritizer-debug) for local dry runs, and docs + examples. Testing: unit tests for prioritizer heuristics, integration smoke that runs on a sampled suite, and a synthetic replay to validate compressor grouping heuristics. Related work: ENG-4123 (probe noise reduction), ENG-4189 (ci alert throttling).
commits: feat(prioritizer): add shard scoring pipeline and sampling policy
feat(compressor): implement failure signature generator and LRU cache
chore(ci): add reliability_score metric + bridge adapter for rate-limited retries
test: add unit tests for scoring heuristics and compressor dedup
docs: add prioritizer guide and config examples
fix(scheduler): ensure stable ordering when priorities tie
reviews: Diego Ramos: Left a few nits on the scoring weights and asked for a short benchmark that shows reduced time-to-detect for high-risk shards. Also asked to ensure the LRU cache is bounded by memory and exposes a clear eviction metric.

Asha Patel: Responded with a microbenchmark (see commits) and added eviction gauges for the compressor. Clarified the default weights in docs and made them configurable via eval_config.prioritizer.weights.
Marta Lee: Requested an integration test that simulates heavy duplicate failures to validate suppression behavior. Noted a small race in scheduler ordering — requested a fix.
Asha Patel: Added deterministic ordering fallback and integration test; CI initially flagged a flaky test in the smoke suite, reran and passed.
Connor Nguyen: Approved after confirming metrics are emitted with stable labels and that the CI adapter does not alter exit codes for non-transient failures.
notes_for_release: opt-in prioritizer available via eval_config.prioritization.enabled; new reliability_score metric emitted under eval.reliability_score; default compressor cooldown is 1h and is configurable via eval_config.compressor.cooldown
qa_notes: Manual QA steps: run `evalctl probe --shard sample --prioritizer` on a 1k prompt set to verify prioritization order, trigger repeated synthetic failures to observe single compressed incident in CI output, and validate reliability_score trend on metrics dashboard.
risk_assessment: Low risk: feature is opt-in and safe by default. Compressor only aggregates and annotates failures; it does not drop raw traces. Memory usage scoped with LRU cap and metrics exported.
